threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—that's a dead giveaway. Locals know the difference when it comes to getting around.
Caught the 35 last night; a guy in Crocs was karaoke-ing to his earbuds like he was on stage at the O2. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in full lederhosen at the corner shop, casually buying a pack of ciggies and some falafel. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find döner shops that double as art galleries, where the kebab tastes like a masterpiece and street art adorns the walls.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they react when BART's down—it's not just a delay, it's a sigh and a roll of the eyes like they've seen it all before.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a woman singing opera on the 47 bus yesterday. Whole bus was silent, even the usual loudmouths. Felt like we shared a secret moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just about the park and squares, but it’s the scent of fresh pa amb tomàquet wafting from corner bars that truly makes it special.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones pulling out Google Maps in the middle of Plaça Reial, oblivious to the street performers and the locals just hanging out.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 106 bus is a reliable option. Real locals know it’s just a suggestion for when you’re looking for a scenic detour.
On the 59 last night, a guy tried to sell me a weed cookie while reciting Shakespeare. Classic Brixton, where art meets the absurd.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? Watching a couple argue in Turkish over a döner while the tram screeched to a halt, blending chaos and culture.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find kebab shops that stay open past sunrise, where locals swap tales over midnight döner like it's a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re local when you can name at least three taco trucks that beat any upscale spot in the city, hands down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a bus driver stop mid-route to help a lost tourist with a map. Muni in chaos, yet moments like this remind you of the city's heart.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always expect late-night tapas spots to be buzzing, but most locals have dinner by 9. By midnight, it’s just us and the drunks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at how the bus schedules seem to change every day, standing there with a printed timetable in hand.
